intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that congenital dyserythropoietic anemia type Ib (CDAN1B) is caused by homozygous mutation in the C15ORF41 gene.

checks.claim: Congenital dyserythropoietic anemia type Ib (CDAN1B) is caused by homozygous mutation in the C15ORF41 gene.
checks.evidence_quote: Homozygous mutations in a predicted endonuclease are a novel cause of congenital dyserythropoietic anemia type I.
checks.explanation: Title and abstract report homozygous C15ORF41 mutations cause CDA I in CDAN1-negative cases; 'type Ib' is nomenclature.

paragraphs.text: The congenital dyserythropoietic anemias are a heterogeneous group of rare disorders that mainly affect erythropoiesis. They show characteristic morphologic abnormalities and a block in erythroid maturation (Babbs et al., 2013). Mutations in the CDAN1 gene cause most cases of congenital dyserythropoietic anemia type I. Type Ib is caused by mutations in C15ORF41, a gene of previously unknown function, in some CDAN1 mutation-negative cases (Babbs et al., 2013). Some patients with CDA type I have been reported with nonhematologic features, including distal limb anomalies (Sabry et al., 1997).

paragraphs.text: Sabry et al. (1997) described dysmorphic features in 3 Bedouin sibs with congenital dyserythropoietic anemia type I. The features were growth retardation/short stature, congenital ptosis, abnormal tarsal bones, metatarsal duplication/hypoplasia, nail/phalangeal hypoplasia of the fingers and toes, Madelung deformity, syndactyly of the toes, and hallux valgus. Peripheral blood lymphocyte cultures from the patients had a very low mitotic index. The phenotype varied among the 3 sibs. Sabry et al. (1997) concluded that their report confirmed an association between a subset of CDA type I and a specific form of distal limb anomalies. They suggested that congenital ptosis and a low mitotic index might also be part of the syndrome profile. The abstract did not say whether this family's disease was due to mutation in C15ORF41.

paragraphs.text: Babbs et al. (2013) studied a consanguineous pedigree of Middle Eastern origin with CDA type I. Using whole-genome sequencing and segregation analysis, they found a homozygous c.533T-A transversion in the C15ORF41 gene, predicted to cause a leu178-to-gln (L178Q) substitution. They then sequenced C15ORF41 in other CDAN1 mutation-negative CDA type I pedigrees. In 2 further pedigrees of Southeast Asian origin, they found a homozygous c.281A-G transition, predicted to cause a tyr94-to-cys (Y94C) substitution. The haplotype surrounding the c.281A-G change suggested a founder effect for this mutation in Pakistan. Detailed sequence similarity searches indicated that C15ORF41 encodes a novel restriction endonuclease belonging to the Holliday junction resolvase family of proteins.
